components.label: Notebook UI
components.responsibility: Own user intent and visible local state; do not make server revisions.

components.label: Notebook backend
components.responsibility: Expose revisioned edits, execution and synchronization.

components.label: Notebook API
components.responsibility: Authenticate, validate revisions and apply notebook transactions.

components.label: Notebook database
components.responsibility: Commit cells, revision counter, operation receipts and change rows atomically.

components.label: Notebook change log
components.responsibility: Ordered rows in the same database transaction as cell changes.

components.label: Optimistic edit handler
components.responsibility: Track pending edits until a matching receipt or authoritative update.

components.label: Live update reducer
components.responsibility: Apply events only in contiguous server revision order.

components.label: Catch-up reducer
components.responsibility: Apply reset snapshots and resumed change batches without restarting jobs.

components.label: Snapshot reader
components.responsibility: Read cells and revision in one consistent database snapshot.

components.label: Subscription hub
components.responsibility: Tail durable changes, authorize subscribers and bound per-client queues.

components.label: Execution outbox dispatcher
components.responsibility: Dispatch committed execution IDs; duplicate delivery is allowed.

components.label: Execution worker
components.responsibility: Claim execution IDs once; publish versioned outputs and terminal state.

components.label: Notebook access policy
components.responsibility: Check membership and revoke active subscriptions when access changes.

components.label: Fenced editing leases
components.responsibility: Allocate monotonic fencing tokens using database transactions and database time.

components.label: Conditional change poller
components.responsibility: One outstanding bounded poll; carry the last applied revision.

components.label: Unified client reconciler
components.responsibility: One owner reconciles receipts, pushes, polling and snapshots.

requirements.text: Server owns cell revisions, execution state and output sequence; clients may show explicit pending edits.
Initial snapshot plus subsequent updates has no gap; reconnect resumes or explicitly resets when history expired.
Retrying one execution operation never starts a second job; reconnect never resubmits a job.
Every request and ongoing subscription enforces notebook membership; slow subscribers consume bounded memory.

problem.scope: Whole-cell edits use revision checks, not character-level OT/CRDT. Study snapshot/update subscriptions and execution state; transport delivery is at least once.

provenance.note: Authored interview preparation. Technical references support mechanisms, not the claim that a company asked this question.

references.supports: Snapshot resource versions, resumed watches and expired-history recovery.
references.title: Kubernetes list/watch semantics

references.supports: Incremental client synchronization is a protocol, not merely a WebSocket connection.
references.title: Matrix client/server sync

acceptanceCases.given: Cell revision is 8; two editors read 8.
acceptanceCases.then: Exactly one commits revision 9; the other receives conflict and does not overwrite it.
acceptanceCases.when: Both submit different replacement text with expectedRevision=8.

acceptanceCases.given: Execution request K was committed but its acknowledgement was lost.
acceptanceCases.then: The original executionId is returned; no second queue job is created.
acceptanceCases.when: Retry K with identical cell revision.

acceptanceCases.given: Snapshot is pinned at revision 10 while revision 11 commits.
acceptanceCases.then: Install snapshot 10, apply 11 once, and finish at revision 11.
acceptanceCases.when: Deliver event 11 before the snapshot, then duplicate 11 after it.

acceptanceCases.given: Client cursor is 4; retained events begin at 20.
acceptanceCases.then: Explicit reset supplies a new snapshot; no execution is resubmitted.

acceptanceCases.given: A live subscriber loses notebook membership.
acceptanceCases.then: Order the revocation in the notebook log; stop later revisions before sending. Previously transmitted events cannot be recalled.

guarantees: No receipt is acknowledged before its cell and change row commit.
Submission retries reuse one job identity; this is not exactly-once arbitrary code execution.
Duplicate acknowledgements and updates never duplicate execution.

assumptions: Text collaboration means whole-cell replacement with visible conflicts.
Execution deduplication uses a durable operation identity and an explicit retry policy.
solutions.chooseWhen: Low update latency matters and the service can operate long-lived subscriptions.

stages.explanation: Separate user intent from authoritative state before adding collaboration. A pending edit is not a committed revision. [Collaborative editing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operational_transformation) must reconcile concurrent edits against an agreed document version. Sending changes is only one part; reconnects also need a way to recover missing updates and conflicts. Consider this case: Cell revision is 8; two editors read 8. Both submit different replacement text with expectedRevision=8.
invariants: A pending edit is not a committed revision.
stages.question: Who owns a cell and what does completion mean?
stages.reason: Separate user intent from authoritative state before adding collaboration.
stages.title: State the notebook boundary

stages.explanation: Make the API/database transaction boundary visible without changing the outer notebook identity. Cells and operation receipts commit together. [Collaborative editing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operational_transformation) must reconcile concurrent edits against an agreed document version. Sending changes is only one part; reconnects also need a way to recover missing updates and conflicts. Consider this case: Execution request K was committed but its acknowledgement was lost.
invariants: Cells and operation receipts commit together.
stages.question: Where are revision checks and durable records stored?
stages.reason: Make the API/database transaction boundary visible without changing the outer notebook identity.
stages.title: Expand the authoritative backend

stages.explanation: The client tracks tentative changes rather than overwriting authoritative revisions. A rejected pending edit remains distinguishable from committed code. [An optimistic interface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optimistic_replication) shows a tentative result before the server confirms it. Pending state must remain distinguishable from authoritative state so rejection or late replies can be reconciled. Consider this case: Cell revision is 8; two editors read 8.
invariants: A rejected pending edit remains distinguishable from committed code.
stages.question: What if an edit is rejected after the UI displayed it?
stages.reason: The client tracks tentative changes rather than overwriting authoritative revisions.
stages.title: Add explicit optimistic state

stages.explanation: A durable execution identity is handed to workers through committed outbox records. A request receipt and execution ID survive retries. [Transaction guarantees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACID) describe which changes become visible together and what survives failure. They must be tied to explicit storage behavior rather than inferred from a successful API call. Consider this case: Execution request K was committed but its acknowledgement was lost.
invariants: A request receipt and execution ID survive retries.
A worker claim does not by itself make arbitrary external effects exactly once.
stages.question: How do retry and reconnect avoid running a cell twice?
stages.reason: A durable execution identity is handed to workers through committed outbox records.
stages.title: Separate execution from reconnect

stages.explanation: Use the snapshot revision as a durable cursor rather than subscribing after an unversioned read. Install snapshot at V, then apply only contiguous events after V. [A snapshot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snapshot_isolation) gives one read operation a fixed view of data. Later writes may change the live system without changing the rows that reader sees.
invariants: Install snapshot at V, then apply only contiguous events after V.
stages.question: How do updates committed during initial loading remain visible?
stages.reason: Use the snapshot revision as a durable cursor rather than subscribing after an unversioned read.
stages.title: Join a snapshot to live updates

stages.explanation: Resume within retention; otherwise obtain a new snapshot and replace the local view explicitly. Cursor expiry is reset, not silent omission. [A cursor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cursor_%28databases%29) records where a query should continue. Its ordering fields must distinguish equal values, and its validity depends on the query and access permissions. Consider this case: Client cursor is 4; retained events begin at 20.
invariants: Cursor expiry is reset, not silent omission.
A recovered view does not create a new execution request.
stages.question: What if a tab returns after history was compacted?
stages.reason: Resume within retention; otherwise obtain a new snapshot and replace the local view explicitly.
stages.title: Recover an expired cursor

stages.explanation: Use explicit membership revisions and bounded buffers; disconnect and resnapshot when a lossless stream cannot keep up. Membership changes are ordered with cell events; later revisions cannot be delivered under revoked access. Already transmitted data cannot be recalled. [A snapshot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snapshot_isolation) gives one read operation a fixed view of data. Later writes may change the live system without changing the rows that reader sees.
invariants: Membership changes are ordered with cell events; later revisions cannot be delivered under revoked access. Already transmitted data cannot be recalled.
Dropping arbitrary execution events is not a valid coalescing policy.
stages.question: What happens when membership changes or a consumer is slow?
stages.reason: Use explicit membership revisions and bounded buffers; disconnect and resnapshot when a lossless stream cannot keep up.
stages.title: Bound and authorize delivery

stages.explanation: One client state owner deduplicates opIds and orders revisions across all transports. Only the unified reducer mutates the displayed authoritative notebook. [Collaborative editing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operational_transformation) must reconcile concurrent edits against an agreed document version. Sending changes is only one part; reconnects also need a way to recover missing updates and conflicts. Consider this case: Execution request K was committed but its acknowledgement was lost.
invariants: Only the unified reducer mutates the displayed authoritative notebook.

operations.reason: Replace competing writers to the same visible cell state with one revision-aware reconciler.

stages.question: Can a receipt, push and catch-up response apply the same change three times?
stages.reason: One client state owner deduplicates opIds and orders revisions across all transports.
stages.title: Merge the competing client reducers

solutions.title: Revision log and server push
tradeoffs: Keep a change-log retention window and operate bounded connection buffers.
A server revision serializes whole-cell writes; conflicting edits require user resolution.

stages.explanation: A lease is useful only when every write validates its fencing token in the same transaction. An expired or superseded fencing token cannot update a cell. [Fencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fencing_%28computing%29) prevents an outdated owner from continuing to modify shared resources. A newer owner needs a token that the resource checks, not merely a belief that ownership changed.
invariants: An expired or superseded fencing token cannot update a cell.
stages.question: Can an expired editor still write?
stages.reason: A lease is useful only when every write validates its fencing token in the same transaction.
stages.title: Serialize editing with fenced leases
